supplementalReferences.name: mitm-dev
supplementalReferences.scope: Request and MITM certificate design only; maintained independently of the overall UI, Android and sing-box baselines. Local paths are relative to the repository root.

files.changes: GPL-3.0 license included in exported CA modules.
Unmodified installer entry, moved to its ZIP path.
Unmodified installer marker, moved to its ZIP path.

Reference for system/Conscrypt APEX and init/zygote/app mount namespaces. B-box patches Zygotes before discovering all visible mount namespaces, deduplicates each scan by namespace identity, rechecks actual stores on every pass, pins namespace/root/interpreter/script/public-CA descriptors before nsenter, stages complete per-store tmpfs copies in /dev, retains hash collisions, and returns pending/failure results. No live stale-certificate removal.
Uses the B-box injector's non-waiting --early pass and resets this boot's diagnostic log; readiness retries belong to service.sh.

Runs one flock-protected reconciliation loop, retries boot readiness every two seconds for at most 60 fast passes, then checks late/recreated namespaces and replaced stores every 30 seconds until disabled/removed. Records the latest exit status and bounded changed-result logs.

Reference for Android CA identity, hash names, store/namespace limitations and public module export. B-box implements non-exportable Keystore signing, revision checks and AtomicFile persistence; no automatic root command or private-key export.
Distinguish user/system trust and refresh after returning from settings. B-box queries its local Android bridge and isolates remote sessions.

Reference for explicit CA operations and certificate setup. B-box uses independent profile MITM with an ordered allowlist (empty decrypts nothing), exclusions, HTTP/2 and HTTP/3 controls, and optional TLS/TCP streams. One certificate entry precedes the decryption controls on a compact MITM page; domain values appear only in the secondary editor, and certificate access does not require a loaded profile. JSON editing covers additional ports/packages settings. HTTP rewriting and HTTP/stream/cron/event/generic scripts are separate B-box extensions. Stream handlers edit TCP chunks or complete WebSocket messages through the B-box message contract and never use task-script run menus. Certificate rotation is blocked during capture or active MITM. Shared form/navigation components are reused; no Mihomo configuration.

Reference for HTTP exchange information. B-box combines current sing-box connections and all retained HTTP, TCP stream/chunk and WebSocket message summaries in one request viewer, following Surge's documented recent/active request model. Independent exchange IDs and optional original connection UUIDs support one-to-many association, filtered deduplication and historical requests without a live parent. Stream IDs, parent records, message directions, opcodes, injection and drop markers come from the B-box core. Pagination affects presentation, not search or export coverage. Body counts remain separate from socket traffic; raw TCP recording is a local setting and MITM remains profile-controlled. No profile-rewrite banner or dedicated capture logs.

Reference for per-message navigation. B-box shares a detail page between ordinary connections and captured records, with copyable connection metadata, related exchanges and HTTP request/response/cookie menus. Expired parents retain observed information without an active close action; closing a captured request's underlying socket explicitly confirms interruption of every request on it. Raw TCP and TLS/TCP aggregate streams have two byte directions; TCP chunks and WebSocket messages show their own direction and optional parent navigation without HTTP headers, cookies or cURL export. Active B-box streams expose independently implemented text/Hex/Base64 injection, WebSocket text/binary opcode selection and request-specific cancellation through the Android bridge. Completed messages refresh while their stream remains active. Parsed HTTP requests add an independently implemented replay form that submits only edited method, URL, header and body fields through the Android bridge with request-specific cancellation and opens the new record. The request list links to independently implemented breakpoint pages for in-memory rules and held HTTP messages, whose request or response fields are edited before continuing or aborting. Domain-only observations have no HTTP message menus.
FEATURE_MITM is disabled by default in this reference. The public FlClash core is not used as an MITM backend.

supplementalReferences.name: captured-body-viewing
supplementalReferences.scope: Automatic captured body classification, complete file-backed JSON and schema-free Protobuf/gRPC interpretation, hexadecimal rows and full body viewing within request/response details. Maintained independently of the overall UI, Android and sing-box baselines. Local paths are relative to the repository root.

files.changes: Rework text/image/binary classification and hexadecimal rows around native byte pages. Automatically identify display formats from the first decoded original page using actual image signatures, valid text/JSON, supported protocol declarations and conservative complete-page untyped Protobuf inference. Validate JSON against decoded text before display-only control replacement. Split JSON uses recognizable container prefixes, or declared JSON string/scalar/whitespace prefixes while excluding obvious HTML/plain text. Readable long text with misleading image MIME remains text on later pages. Invalid encodings, empty/error pages and raw saved-byte fallback provide no full-view format; unknown binary stays hexadecimal. Preserve Text/Encoding and absolute original byte offsets while accepting separately decoded native charset/displayText fields, including ASCII pages in non-UTF-8 charsets. Validate canonical Base64 and Unicode, replace only sparse display controls, and retain bytes for unsupported charsets. Native default UTF-8 preserves untyped binary Protobuf inference. Dart retains bounded single-page quick parsing; healthy decoded first-page hints allow complete, nonempty, untruncated directions to open native image files or streamed JSON/Protobuf/gRPC text files within the request/response detail body, independently of the original page's source and offsets. These hints are candidates; native full-file HTTP decoding and text format validation can still fail while retaining the original page for fallback and retry. Existing B-box JSON formatting preserves numbers, duplicate keys and escapes; Flutter keeps only its current original and derived pages.

Implement schema-free numbered fields, repeated values, unsigned 64-bit integers, fixed-width hexadecimal values and inferred text/nested/opaque length-delimited fields. The Dart quick path keeps depth 16, 4096-node and 64 KiB derived-output budgets and falls back to original page bytes for incomplete, invalid or over-budget structures. The adapted Go ReaderAt path validates complete decoded files and streams all fields and frames to UTF-8 view files without the Dart node or total-output budgets, while retaining depth 16 for nesting inference and byte summaries for opaque fields. Support multiple gRPC frames, gRPC-Web binary or independently padded Base64 blocks, and trailers. Declared gRPC +json messages are validated as JSON, with invalid messages displayed as hexadecimal bytes while retaining outer framing and omitting the Protobuf schema notice. The quick path retains compressed message bytes and their declared encoding; the complete path decodes supported grpc-encoding values independently of outer HTTP compression and retains byte summaries when message decoding is unsupported or fails. Capture retention and original export bytes remain independent of both display paths.

Reference for text/image/hex viewing, wrapping and original byte access. B-box uses Prism cards and controls for automatically selected full body viewing and operations directly within request/response details, with responsive lazy hex rows, content-dependent wrapping/horizontal scrolling, image zoom/reset, original-page copying and a body menu for displayed-content copying. Each body State owns a CapturedBodyReader, a ChangeNotifier that holds the direction-bound native reader and all page, format and paging state while the widget keeps visibility, scrolling, zoom, wrapping, copying and layout. The reader retains initial-page format recognition across original and derived pages, and receives live metadata from the parent detail poll; appended tails refresh without resetting page history, older replies are rejected, and transient truncation can clear after a pending write. A healthy decoded first page with current counters replaces an earlier raw first page after canceling its reader and pending work. Later raw byte pages retain their source, offsets and history while using separate healthy first-page hints for complete viewing; returning to the raw first page permits decoded rebinding. Keep-alive state retains the original page and derived view when scrolling beyond the list cache. Complete decoded images use file providers with aspect-preserving bounded decode dimensions, error-to-hex fallback and cache eviction. Complete JSON/Protobuf/gRPC view files use separate UTF-8 byte offsets and history without changing original counts or copied Text/Base64. Hidden, backgrounded, disposed or obsolete-session readers cancel work and clean temporary files; active bodies recreate readers and restore derived pages, while old-session data stays inaccessible. Prism provides controls within the existing detail navigation.

Reference edge cases for body types, declared charset, malformed/truncated text and hexadecimal layout. B-box adds initial-page format recognition, actual image signatures and readable content with absent or misleading MIME, native charset display fields across pages, equal ASCII display/original text for legacy charsets, default UTF-8 untyped inference, latest direction metadata, completeness/source boundaries, exact original byte preservation, responsive absolute offsets, wire-format validity and single-page quick-parser budgets. Detail-body tests additionally cover automatic full viewing and operations in place, stable format recognition across pages, live tail refresh, transient truncation recovery, complete file and derived-page views, unknown-binary fallback, separated byte/history/copy semantics and reader cancellation/restoration. Tests are included in the existing GitHub Actions Flutter job; source presence does not claim a passing run.
